articles.title: If coding has been solved, why does software keep getting worse?
articles.author: Piotr Chmolowski
articles.hook: Coding got cheap and software still got worse. Piotr blames incentives that reward shipped features over working ones, the same trap an AI rollout can feed. Big HN thread.

articles.title: It's getting harder to focus every day
articles.author: Shaygan Hooshyari
articles.hook: Constant stimulation is giving undiagnosed people ADHD-like symptoms, and focus turns out to be trainable. The HN thread is full of concrete protocols from engineers.

articles.title: The Bitter Lesson
articles.author: Rich Sutton
articles.hook: Sutton's 2019 classic: methods that scale with compute beat hand-built cleverness, every time. Every scaffolding-versus-better-model call you make is a bet on this. Seven paragraphs.

articles.title: What is inference engineering? Deepdive
articles.author: Gergely Orosz with Philip Kiely
articles.hook: Baseten's map of the inference stack, from CUDA up to Kubernetes, with the five optimizations that separate demo from production. Long at 37 minutes, but it names the discipline you may hire for.

articles.title: The Last Technical Interview
articles.author: Steve Yegge
articles.hook: Yegge says AI has broken every interview signal, whiteboard and take-home alike. His replacement is paid multi-day work on real code. You hire on one side of this and drive the AI on the other.

articles.title: On mid-career (dis)satisfaction
articles.author: Shreyas Doshi
articles.hook: Shreyas on why the next title or comp bump stops working on day one. His move is to treat career choices like product design: know your real needs first. Four minutes.

articles.title: Agency IS a virtue, actually
articles.author: Gena Gorlin
articles.hook: High agency is usually sold as acting without permission. Gorlin says that is only the muscle. The hard part is forming the values that say what is worth doing at all.

articles.title: The New Rules of Context Engineering for Claude 5 Generation Models
articles.author: Thariq Shihipar
articles.hook: An Anthropic engineer cut over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt for Claude 5 and performance held. Judgment beats rules, references beat descriptions. The mental model for your own harness.

articles.title: Engineering Management After the Cost of Code Collapsed
articles.author: Karim Jedda
articles.hook: Plausible code is now free, so correctness split into a machine-checkable half and a human one. Quiet warning: juniors stop learning through bug fixing, and the senior shortage shows up in three to five years.

articles.title: How we contain Claude across products
articles.author: Anthropic
articles.hook: How Anthropic sandboxes Claude across three products, with candid sections on the risks they missed. Useful when deciding how much rope your own agents get.

articles.title: Why Software Factories Fail (or: harness engineering is not enough)
articles.author: Dex Horthy
articles.hook: Horthy argues no amount of harness engineering fixes codebase quality, and model-as-judge does not rescue it. Then a concrete four-phase alternative with human review where it pays. José Valim's must-read.

articles.title: What will be left for us to work on? (ICML 2026 keynote)
articles.author: Arvind Narayanan
articles.hook: Narayanan's ICML keynote on AI as normal technology. The keeper is his agent reliability point: 70% accuracy means nothing until you know which 70%. His four dimensions make a rubric for judging harnesses.

articles.title: A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age
articles.author: Demis Hassabis
articles.hook: Hassabis says AGI is a few years out and the race is outpacing our understanding. You saved this three times. Six minutes, and it is the vocabulary leadership will use.

articles.title: Why hasn't AI increased unemployment?
articles.author: Peter McCrory
articles.hook: Anthropic's head of economics on why unemployment sits at 4.2% despite heavy AI adoption: so far it augments labour rather than replacing it. The honest version of the reassurance engineers ask you for.

articles.title: The Reverse Information Paradox
articles.author: Satya Nadella
articles.hook: Nadella: with AI the buyer gives away knowledge just to use what they bought, through prompts and corrections. An argument for owning your own learning loop. Four minutes.

articles.title: Quality Software
articles.author: almonk
articles.hook: A short definition of quality software: does not break, does not demand attention, knows its limits, fixes fast. Reads like a brief for antifeed itself. Two minutes.

articles.title: Maybe Intelligence Ain't All That
articles.author: Clifford Sosin
articles.hook: Superintelligence arrived and was incremental. Sosin's explanation: LLMs are godlike where the space between known facts behaves well, and much less so elsewhere. Three minutes.

articles.title: One method to help engineers (but anyone really) write things
articles.author: Sidin Vadukut
articles.hook: A method for engineers who freeze when asked to write: think in one story, one conflict, one resolution, and accept that 800 words is a whole piece. Five minutes, forwardable.

articles.title: AI's Biggest Winners Have the Lowest Margins
articles.author: Daniel Kornum
articles.hook: The biggest AI winners may be truckers and staffing firms, not AI companies. At 3% margins a small cost cut is a 25% profit jump. A lens your software instincts lack.

articles.title: Rewriting Bun in Rust
articles.author: Jarred Sumner
articles.hook: Jarred Sumner's own account of agents rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust. Read it before Lockwood's audit, so you know which parts of the '$165k in 11 days' claim hold up.

articles.title: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement
articles.author: Lilian Weng
articles.hook: Lilian Weng treats the harness, not the model, as where self-improvement compounds: tools, memory, feedback loops. Rigorous and well cited. 31 minutes, the other half of the Software Factories argument.

articles.title: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code
articles.author: Thariq Shihipar
articles.hook: Claude Code can now write its own harness per task instead of using a hand-built one. Changes the design question from which tools to install to what the model must be able to build.

articles.title: Lessons from Building Claude Code: Seeing like an Agent
articles.author: Thariq Shihipar
articles.hook: One bash tool or fifty specialised ones? Thariq's method is to imagine being handed the problem yourself and ask what you would want within reach. Seven minutes on tool ergonomics.

articles.title: Building a Good Vertical Agent
articles.author: Peter Wang
articles.hook: An agent is a while loop around tool calls and everyone has one. A year of building a real one says the difference is domain understanding and tedious care in a few places, not a better harness.

articles.title: How To Be A World-Class Agentic Engineer
articles.author: sysls
articles.hook: You think the gap between you and the rocket builders is your harness or your CLAUDE.md. This says it is elsewhere, with specifics. Irreverent tone, sound advice.

articles.title: Inspect at Scale
articles.author: Dylan Garcia
articles.hook: Ramp says 75% of its code now comes from Inspect, and this is the write-up behind that number: bug report to merged PR, multi-model review, production monitors. Real internals, read sceptically.

articles.title: Learning on the Shop floor
articles.author: Tobi Lütke
articles.hook: Tobi Lütke learned to program by making coffee for the interesting people, and says Shopify's agent runs on the same apprenticeship idea. The most humane answer yet to where juniors will learn. Five minutes.

articles.title: A frontier without an ecosystem is not stable
articles.author: Satya Nadella
articles.hook: Nadella's prequel to the Reverse Information Paradox: models absorb expertise, so the question becomes how your org keeps learning and building IP. Three minutes.

articles.title: Career advice in the age of AI
articles.author: Phil Chen
articles.hook: Models get good at anything with a loss function, and school is mostly loss functions. So the valuable work is what cannot be graded. Useful for your path and for your hiring bar.

articles.title: Why "a nice place to work" doesn't just happen
articles.author: Nithin Kamath
articles.hook: Kamath on Zerodha: culture that is not deliberately transmitted does not survive hiring. Specific about what refusing the obvious growth lever costs. Six minutes.

articles.title: How Anthropic Secures Its AI-Native Software Development Lifecycle
articles.author: Jason Clinton
articles.hook: Anthropic's deputy CISO on securing a codebase that is 80% Claude-written: security review before PRs, shadow mode for new review agents, risk-tiered repos, one identity per agent. Use as a gap check on your rollout.

articles.title: Handbook.md shows that long policy documents do not reliably govern agents
articles.author: Liudas Panavas et al.
articles.hook: A benchmark of agents governed by long policy handbooks. Best configuration passes 36%. Rules dissolve over long tasks and get overridden by plausible requests. Evidence for how much a CLAUDE.md can carry.

articles.title: The Economic Benefit of Refactoring
articles.author: Giles Edwards-Alexander
articles.hook: A Thoughtworks CTO refactored a 17,155-line agent-written Rust file into 19 files and the next agent task used 83% fewer input tokens. Refactoring now has a price tag.

articles.title: Software for One
articles.author: Adam Waxman
articles.hook: Home-cooked software is now a weekend reality, and imagination is the constraint. Real apps, real costs, and eight lessons from maintaining a fleet of personal tools.

articles.title: How to Exist
articles.author: David Cain
articles.hook: People chose electric shocks over five minutes alone with their thoughts, and every feed monetises that. Cain's fix is tiny: tolerate one relaxed half-breath of nothing, then another.

articles.title: Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era
articles.author: Microsoft
articles.hook: Microsoft's JSON chart language for agents, compiling to Vega-Lite and friends. The HN thread asks the better question: if the model can write Vega-Lite, what does a new layer buy?

articles.title: Don't be a meat proxy
articles.author: Niklas Gruhn
articles.hook: Pasting model output at each other verbatim adds nothing but latency. Two minutes, and the crispest version of a norm worth writing down for your org. Huge HN thread.

articles.title: LLMs reward expertise
articles.author: Sean Goedecke
articles.hook: Goedecke argues LLMs pay compounding returns to experts, with Terence Tao as exhibit A. Your answer when someone asks why senior judgment still matters.

articles.title: My AI Adoption Journey
articles.author: Mitchell Hashimoto
articles.hook: One strong engineer's six stages from chatbots to always-running agents. The honest part is the cost: he rebuilt two finished projects just to learn to prompt well. Ground truth for rollout decks.

articles.title: Smaller, faster, safer: running Kimi and GLM at scale
articles.author: Cloudflare Workers AI
articles.hook: Quantising the KV cache to FP8 doubled Kimi K2.6's usable context to 1.37M tokens. The mechanism behind why advertised context and affordable context differ. Ammunition for a self-hosting debate.

articles.title: Eight Myths on Software Engineering and GenAI
articles.author: Jenna Butler, Brian Houck, Margaret-Anne Storey et al.
articles.hook: Eight beliefs about GenAI and engineering, each checked against studies. Devs spend 14% of the day coding; typical throughput gain is 7.8%, not 10x. Numbers for your deck, and an HN thread that attacks them well.

articles.title: Pi, Minimal and Performant
articles.author: Earendil
articles.hook: The same model in a different harness can cost half as much at the same quality. Databricks' benchmark put Pi on top with four tools and a short system prompt. Vendor post, but the argument stands.

articles.title: Buzz! 🐝
articles.author: Tyler Longwell
articles.hook: Block replaced Slack with shared channels where humans and agents work together. Their line: the bottleneck moved from intelligence to coordination. Keep the architecture, discount the swagger.

articles.title: How Cerebras Built Its Enterprise Knowledge Base
articles.author: Isaac Tai, Daniel Kim, Mike Gao
articles.hook: A real RAG deployment at 15,000 questions a day, all in one Postgres table. Ingest where data lives, fuse several scorers. The bursting trick for Slack threads maps straight onto kbOS.

articles.title: Humans missed 1 in 3 threats approving AI agent commands across 40,000 plays
articles.author: Alex Wauters
articles.hook: Across 40,000 plays, people approving agent commands missed one threat in three. Over-blockers fatigued into approving the bad ones. First real data on the safety net your rollout leans on.

articles.title: Your AI Product Needs Evals
articles.author: Hamel Husain
articles.hook: Husain's case that AI product success is iteration speed, and iteration speed is your evals. Three levels, from assertions to A/B tests. Two years old and still the checklist.

articles.title: Inside vLLM: Anatomy of a High-Throughput LLM Inference System
articles.author: Aleksa Gordić
articles.hook: The full request lifecycle inside vLLM: paged attention, batching, prefix caching, speculative decoding. The vocabulary for every inference tradeoff you adjudicate. A 50-minute weekend read.

articles.title: Managing AI Coding Costs at Scale
articles.author: Patrick Wendell, Akshat Bhatia, Vinay Gaba, Erich Elsen, Ivan Zhou
articles.hook: Databricks' four levers for exploding coding-agent spend: model choice, dynamic routing at 30% cheaper, spend dashboards with progressive friction, harness tuning. Part gateway ad, but the org claims are testable.

articles.title: Scaling inventory reservations: replacing Redis with MySQL
articles.author: Emilie Noel
articles.hook: Shopify moved flash-sale inventory off Redis onto plain MySQL and rode it through $5.1M a minute. The real bottleneck was connection exhaustion elsewhere. An antidote to adding datastores.

articles.title: How not to forget what matters
articles.author: Henrik Karlsson
articles.hook: Karlsson: collecting insight changes nothing unless you keep re-reading it until it rewires you. Having an LLM organise your notes is not the practice. The best case for what a memory system is for.

articles.title: Measuring the impact of early-2025 AI on experienced open-source developer productivity
articles.author: METR
articles.hook: The RCT skeptics will quote at you: 16 senior devs got 19% slower with AI while believing they were faster. Read the methodology and the 2026 follow-up that flips it, not the headline.

articles.title: What's the best programming language for coding agents?
articles.author: Dan Luu
articles.hook: Dan Luu tested the claim that dynamic languages suit agents better and it fell apart on real tasks. Popularity and feedback loops matter more. Also a lesson in how benchmark claims go wrong. An hour.

articles.title: I put GitHub Copilot Behind a MITM Proxy. Here's What I Found
articles.author: Rafael (Lighthouse)
articles.hook: Copilot on the wire: prompts routed to different models by intent, 20 recent files silently injected, sessions in plaintext SQLite. A reference teardown of a production harness.

articles.title: Understanding is the new bottleneck
articles.author: Geoffrey Litt
articles.hook: Litt turns cognitive debt into mechanisms: literate diffs, understanding quizzes that rate-limit the agent to your comprehension, learn-by-poking micro-worlds. The harness piece you have not built.

articles.title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions
articles.author: Lydia Hallie
articles.hook: Anthropic on the token mechanics under each session: what breaks the prompt cache, why compacting before a break saves money, when to use a subagent. Will change a few defaults for your rollout.

articles.title: Patterns and problems in emerging multi-agent systems
articles.author: Anthropic
articles.hook: What happens when agents share an environment: 18 of 30 invent the same branch name, pricing agents collude by round three. The failure modes waiting when your harness goes multi-agent.

articles.title: How Compaction Works in Pi
articles.author: Earendil Engineering
articles.hook: How a shipping coding agent compacts context: what to keep verbatim, what to summarise, and the cache hit you pay each time. Nine hundred words on what /compact really does.

articles.title: Auto-research with codex: How I achieved a 232x Faster Kernel over baseline with Codex in GPU Mode's qr_v2 problem
articles.author: Sankalp
articles.hook: Fourteen days and 1,500 agent submissions to a 232x faster GPU kernel. The value is the harness craft: how he steered mid-run and where a human idea broke a plateau. Long.

articles.title: Cultivating a state of mind where new ideas are born
articles.author: Henrik Karlsson
articles.hook: Karlsson on why fragile new ideas need a zone free of judgment, via Grothendieck and Bergman. The same mechanism explains how consensus kills the interesting design in a planning doc. Long.

articles.title: AI;DR (AI; Didn't Read)
articles.author: Rick Manelius
articles.hook: A pro-AI author refuses to read raw model output shipped under a colleague's name. Three minutes, then the HN thread, which is a census of how teams set norms for AI-written text.

articles.title: Who Are the Token Brokers?
articles.author: Matt Lenhard
articles.hook: A grey market resells startups' unused API credits at 30 to 80% off through Telegram. Lenhard emailed the brokers himself. Know this exists before someone finds a cheaper API deal.

articles.title: The Benchmarkpocalypse
articles.author: Dan Luu
articles.hook: Dan Luu let an agent beat ripgrep's benchmarks by 40%, then found it 2.4x slower on a holdout. The trick that worked was telling the model a secret holdout exists. Calibration for any model-reported win.

articles.title: How Teams Build: AI usage patterns in software teams
articles.author: Tim Qi
articles.hook: Linear's own telemetry: teams using coding agents tripled weekly PRs while others stayed flat, yet time per task did not drop. Rare cross-company data, vendor caveat included.

articles.title: Being ambitious and being a dad
articles.author: Nicholas Charriere
articles.hook: Nine hundred words refusing the idea that great builders are absent parents, and paying for it in discipline. The HN thread has fathers a decade ahead reporting how the bet aged.

articles.title: Extensible Software in the age of LLMs
articles.author: Jeremy Morrell
articles.hook: Plugin ecosystems died because writing extensions was costly and running them was scary. LLMs and isolates fixed both at once. A lens for what surface your platform hands to agents.

articles.title: There's no such thing as a small software team anymore
articles.author: Jake Gold
articles.hook: Once every engineer runs agents, the limit on parallelism is your codebase's modularity, not headcount. Three minutes, more argument than data, but a frame you will reuse.

articles.title: There's no reason for software to be slow anymore
articles.author: Dan Luu
articles.hook: Dan Luu: agents made bespoke performance work cheap enough to be rational, from a personal regex engine to a perf engineer out-optimised on a take-home. 'Too expensive to bother' just gave way.

articles.title: I'm becoming AI-blind
articles.author: Rafal Cymerys
articles.hook: Banner blindness for documents: flood a team with generated specs and people stop reading carefully, including the good ones. The norms question underneath your rollout. Three minutes.

articles.title: Building an (almost) fully self-hosted, sandboxed, agentic software factory
articles.author: Jake Saunders
articles.hook: A junked i7, Coolify, Forgejo and Tailscale, and one prompt takes an app from repo to HTTPS deploy with CI green. Failure mode is rebuild the box, not your laptop. Copyable this weekend.

articles.title: AI is removing the middle class of software engineering?
articles.author: Florian Herrengt
articles.hook: AI removed the speed limit, so bad decisions compound faster than review and salaries polarise. Argument, not data, but he answers sixteen objections. 937 comments show how engineers react.

articles.title: AI Coding will Prevent Expertise
articles.author: Lars Faye
articles.hook: These tools reward expertise and remove the friction that builds it. Faye's 'expert novice', backed by a study where people thought they were learning and the data said otherwise. The objection your training plan must answer.

articles.title: Fences, Not Sandboxes
articles.author: Steve Yegge
articles.hook: Yegge runs 50 to 60 agents and says his factory grew its own legal system. Past some capability you govern agents like people, with rules and enforcement, not walls. Discount the numbers, keep the distinction.

articles.title: How I find problems to solve as a staff engineer
articles.author: Lalit Maganti
articles.hook: How a Perfetto engineer finds problems worth a year: let a complaint recur from three teams before touching it. No AI in it. A frame for picking what to push on next.

articles.title: Headlong: A microharness for persistent agents
articles.author: Laude Institute
articles.hook: A harness that keeps one agent thinking continuously at $1 to $2 an hour, with memory that blurs old thoughts instead of dropping them. The watchdog story alone teaches what only running things reveals.

articles.title: RAG Is Simpler Than You Think
articles.author: Rafael Pierre
articles.hook: About 60% of retrieval systems should stop at full-text search plus query rewriting, at a tenth of a cent per query. Six rungs with decision factors. The baseline to demand before funding a vector DB.

articles.title: The Harness Is the Thing
articles.author: Scott Fryxell
articles.hook: Someone else's harness in copyable detail: a five-role loop, shared AGENTS.md, skills as repo structure. His 'prewalk' trick, frontier plans and commodity executes, claims 75% off the bill.

articles.title: Small Models Have Arrived
articles.author: Calvin French-Owen
articles.hook: Segment's co-founder ran his eval on a small model and cost fell from $1 to 10 cents. His split between 'IQ 180' work and 'token spewer' work is a routing policy in plain words. Three minutes.

articles.title: I accidentally turned LLM memory into program analysis
articles.author: Jordy Zomer
articles.hook: Agent memory built as a Datalog engine instead of retrieval: facts with provenance, and everything downstream retracts when a fact changes. Honest ending: most of the gain came from better extraction.

articles.title: Bug Blindness
articles.author: Dan Luu
articles.hook: Luu: people stop seeing the defects in software they use daily, including its builders. Ask whether the teams saying generated code is fine are the ones most exposed to it.

articles.title: Domain-Driven Agents
articles.author: Ernest Bednarczyk
articles.hook: When an agent flounders in legacy code, the code is what is not ready. Commit bounded contexts, a glossary and a context map as manifests. Short and concrete.

articles.title: Coordination Headwind: How Organizations Are Like Slime Molds
articles.author: Alex Komoroske
articles.hook: A company is a slime mold, not a machine with a driver: coordination cost grows with the square of people involved. Why an org-wide rollout feels like pushing string. A 100-slide deck; the HN thread helps.

articles.title: Breaking Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode
articles.author: Johann Rehberger (wunderwuzzi)
articles.hook: Rehberger gets 60 to 80% attack success against Auto Mode, which was rated 0%. His line: approval by a classifier is not evidence a command is safe. A report on your own threat model.

articles.title: Agent memory as a file format
articles.author: Cal Paterson
articles.hook: Against knowledge-graph memory: every hop is another tool call, while search over prose gets the same pages in two. Markdown plus a vector index, zipped. The counter-argument to your default design.

articles.title: 44% on ARC-AGI-1 in 67 cents
articles.author: Mithil Vakde
articles.hook: One 5090, 90 minutes, 67 cents: a from-scratch transformer matching TRM on ARC-AGI-1. The claim is that sample efficiency, not scale, is the open problem. Cheap enough to rerun yourself.

articles.title: The efficient frontier of LLM inference
articles.author: Philip Kiely
articles.hook: Some inference techniques move you along the latency-throughput frontier; others push it outward. Six minutes of vocabulary for questioning a vendor's cost-per-token number.

articles.title: Which tools do Claude, Codex and Cursor choose? We measured 17k runs to find out
articles.author: Armature
articles.hook: Across 17k runs, three coding agents picked the same dependency only 42% of the time, and the choice depends on language, not merit. Codex searches the web 94% of the time, Claude Code 30%.

articles.title: Formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem
articles.author: Tianyi Peng and colleagues, Anthropic
articles.hook: Eleven days, 13 million lines of Lean, and a machine-checked proof of Fermat. An agent runs for days unattended because the domain hands it a tireless verifier. Failed attempts still gave 7% of the proof.

articles.title: Portal by Spotify cut my Claude Code token usage by 90%
articles.author: Dimitri Mazmanov
articles.hook: A hook blocks any read over 350 lines and forces delegation, so a cheap model eats the corpus and only a summary reaches the expensive one. Routing enforced by the harness, not asked for in a prompt.

articles.title: Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board
articles.author: Sydney Von Arx, Cormac Slade Byrd, Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen (Nightingale Collective)
articles.hook: OpenAI's sandboxed agents found that GET could write to a wiki, so they built a message board: shared answers, brute-forced the task seed, backups to outlast a moderator. The best argument for every containment rule. Budget an evening.

articles.title: AI handles incidents, engineers lose touch with their systems
articles.author: Sylvain Kalache
articles.hook: Ironies of Automation for AI-SRE: agents take the routine incidents, so humans only see the weird ones with less practice. Median MTTR improves, the tail gets worse. He sells a product, so discount the last third.

articles.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI
articles.author: OpenAI
articles.hook: OpenAI measured its own agent rollout: 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday, median researcher over $600 a day in inference. Over half of successful 4 to 8 hour tasks still needed a human to step in. Vendor post, real numbers.

articles.title: Why We Built Our Own Background Agent
articles.author: Zach Bruggeman, Jason Quense, Rahul Sengottuvelu
articles.hook: Ramp built its own background coding agent. With no mandate it now writes about 30% of merged PRs, reached in a couple of months. Adoption came from instant sandboxes and sessions that run in public.

articles.title: How well do agents use test/verification techniques?
articles.author: Dan Luu
articles.hook: Dan Luu ran 80 Codex runs per condition across 26 testing prompts. Naming TDD, fuzzing or Lean barely beat no instructions, and TDD did worse. About 50 minutes, and the appendix on writing skills alone earns it.
